page.title: One invite. Three honest outcomes.
page.subtitle: A sponsored fan-event journey that keeps capacity, registration and permission separate.

sections.heading: From fan invitation to the right confirmation
sections.text: Proposed journey, not the Islanders’ deployed stack. Official team imagery; illustrative campaign, records and integrations. Focused app mockups, not account screenshots. A/B mark source-to-screen matches. Clock is illustrative staging.

steps.text: **Show the invitation.** A proposed fan-social campaign uses official Islanders imagery with an explicitly fictional partner. The email’s Reserve my place button leads to event details—not directly to a confirmed reservation.
**Open the event details.** The fan sees the proposed creative, partner placement and RSVP action. No real date, venue or event is being advertised; this is a walkthrough for reviewing the journey.
**Match the creative to its source.** A is the event headline; B is the RSVP button. Contentful’s proposed custom fields line up with the phone, including the example partner credit.

**Make permission a separate choice.** On the available-capacity path, the fan chooses the optional sponsor checkbox. The Eventbrite-style order form is a focused mockup; custom questions can be optional.

**Confirm only a completed registration.** In this simulated outcome the RSVP succeeded. The organizer record shows Registered and sponsor opt-in Yes as separate values. A click on the invitation did not establish either fact.

**Use the confirmed facts.** The proposed integration passes registration and the separate opt-in answer to Marketing Cloud. The fan receives the reservation message; the sponsor audience includes only explicit opt-ins. No sponsor message is sent in this story.

**Leave sponsor opt-in unchecked.** The same optional question stays unanswered/No. The fan can still finish the RSVP. Declining partner marketing must not change the availability or reservation decision in this proposed journey.

**The place is still reserved.** This simulated registration is successful with sponsor opt-in No. Compare the two fields; the fan’s confirmation must not imply that a sponsor subscription was required.

**Send the event message, not sponsor marketing.** The proposed integration carries Registered plus opt-in No. The reservation confirmation still goes out; the fan is excluded from the proposed sponsor audience.
**Capacity changes the action.** Eventbrite supports a waitlist when the configured ticket type or event is full. The fan now sees Join waitlist, not Reserve my place. No place is held at this step.

**A waitlist is not a ticket.** The simulated fan joins the waitlist and sees an honest acknowledgement. Sponsor permission is not collected on this path; no automatic ticket release or reservation is shown.

**Keep follow-up consistent.** The proposed integration carries Waitlisted, not Registered, with sponsor permission Not collected. The fan receives a waitlist message and is excluded from the proposed sponsor audience.
